items.title: The 3 Roles of Context for AI Agents
items.summary: NN/G researchers break down how power users of AI agents organize information into three types — global (brand rules and governance), local (task-specific files), and ambient (raw data streams like emails) — arguing that curating a context library matters more than crafting prompts.
items.why: The global/local/ambient framework is a practical mental model for any design lead starting to work with AI agents; directly applicable to setting up Cuemath's design and product workflows where brand rules, project context, and live data all need to reach the agent.

items.title: Odds' identity for Alaena strikes a soft balance between science and nature
items.summary: Paris studio Odds built the visual identity for Alaena, a dermatologist-founded skincare brand, using laboratory-inspired letterforms, generous tracking, a restrained blue palette, and chrome packaging to make clinical precision feel warm rather than cold.
items.why: A craft-level case study in designing for dual emotional registers — rigor and warmth — which is exactly the tension Cuemath's design system navigates: math as precise and structured, but the experience as encouraging and kid-friendly.

items.title: Test Complex Interactions Earlier with AI Prototyping
items.summary: A five-step guide showing how AI prototyping tools can build high-fidelity, interactive prototypes of complex interfaces — filters, dashboards, conversational systems — fast enough to test with real users before any engineering work begins.
items.why: Cuemath's interactive math exercises and gamified flows are exactly the multi-state, hard-to-prototype interfaces this piece targets; the workflow could cut the gap between design intent and user validation significantly for the practice app.

items.title: Swash #5
items.summary: A folded, offset-printed brochure for a French creative training organization, typeset in three complementary typefaces with metallic inks and spot colors — a compact demonstration of how print constraints force disciplined typographic hierarchy.
items.why: The pairing logic here — geometric sans anchoring display scale, offset by complementary serif details — is a useful reference for Cuemath's editorial content, where display and body type need to work across very different reading contexts.

items.title: AI for No Good Reason
items.summary: Julie Zhuo makes the case for using AI on personal projects with zero productivity justification — exploring hobbies, building what-if scenarios, making one-of-a-kind gifts — arguing that creative agency is itself a sufficient reason to use the technology.
items.why: The reframe matters for a Cuemath design lead thinking about AI in kids' learning: if AI's real power is expanding what you can make for yourself (not just how fast you work), the parallel is kids using AI to express mathematical ideas, not just drill them.

items.title: Source Material: Zach Lieberman Likes to Break Things
items.summary: Creative coder and School for Poetic Computation co-founder Zach Lieberman on iteration, breaking things on purpose, his warning about AI tools that 'stop at the output,' and why 'repeating yourself' is underrated creative advice.
items.why: His critique of AI output without process — that it skips the friction where real learning happens — is directly relevant to how Cuemath should think about AI in a math learning context, where struggle and iteration are the point, not bugs to optimize away.
